title: Tamsin and the Sigil
premise: Tamsin Vale has spent her whole life in the Hollow Valley, a refuge where magic cannot follow — until the night the old gods resume answering prayers and her own forgotten memories begin surfacing as glowing sigils on her skin. Fleeing with Dominic Eriksen, an exiled storm-caller who once broke the covenant between realms, she discovers she is the living seal of that broken pact: her erased childhood was the price the gods paid to keep the realms apart. As divine factions war over who will control the reforged covenant, Tamsin must choose between restoring her stolen memories and sealing the realms forever. In the end she splits the difference — sacrificing the sigil's power to bind the gods to a new covenant written in mortal memory, keeping her past but losing the magic that could have made her more than human.
about_author: Felix Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms before turning to fiction full-time. They write fantasy about memory, debt, and the small violences of survival from a cluttered study overlooking a rain-logged harbor town.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the magic-dead Hollow Valley, Tamsin tends her grandmother's candle shop and notices small wrongnesses: prayers whispered at shrines are suddenly answered. A stranger arrives asking about a girl with a birthmark shaped like a key. The beat is quiet unease — the ordinary world cracking at its seams.

chapters.title: A Storm-Caller Walks In
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Exiled storm-caller Dominic Eriksen crosses into the valley where his magic fails him, hunting rumors of answered prayers. He recognizes Tamsin's sigil-birthmark from covenant lore he helped shatter years ago. The beat is wary recognition: two people who each sense the other knows something forbidden.

chapters.title: What the Shrine Gave Back
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A dying neighbor prays at the old shrine and is inexplicably healed; that night Tamsin dreams a life she never lived — a burning tower, a woman calling her by another name. She wakes with a new sigil inked across her wrist. The beat is vertigo: identity beginning to unspool.

chapters.title: The Warden's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The valley's Warden confronts Dominic with records proving Tamsin was delivered here as a child under terms no one will name. Dominic realizes the valley isn't a refuge — it's a vault, and Tamsin is its contents. The beat is dread dressed as bureaucratic menace.

chapters.title: Running Out of Hollow
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Wardens move to 're-contain' Tamsin; Dominic's storm-magic, dead in the valley, flickers strangely near her sigils. They flee together through the mountain pass as the valley's protective silence begins to fail behind them. The beat is panicked momentum and reluctant trust.

chapters.title: First Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Outside the valley, Tamsin instinctively prays for shelter — and something answers, folding a farmhouse out of mist. The god Veyra appears, calls Tamsin 'the Seal,' and offers her memories back in exchange for service. The beat is seduction: the temptation of a self she never knew.

chapters.title: Debts of the Broken Covenant
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic confesses his exile's cause: he shattered the covenant to save his sister, scattering its binding into a mortal bloodline — Tamsin's. The gods have hunted the seal ever since. The beat is guilt laid bare, and Tamsin's fury at being someone else's collateral.

chapters.title: The God-Market
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the free city of Corvane, mortals trade favors with minor gods in a bazaar of altars. Tamsin learns every answered prayer is a contract, and hers are pre-signed — her sigils are clauses. The beat is dark wonder curdling into exploitation.

chapters.title: Veyra's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Veyra corners Dominic: help deliver the Seal to the conclave of gods, and his exile ends and his sister lives. He refuses — then discovers his sister died years ago, and Veyra knew. The beat is betrayal, and the hardening of his loyalty to Tamsin over any god.

chapters.title: Sigils Rising
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Each use of her power burns another memory away; Tamsin can no longer recall her grandmother's face. She keeps a mundane journal against the erosion, writing herself down like scripture. The beat is grief — the price of survival paid in installments of self.

chapters.title: The Conclave of Ash
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Rival god-factions convene at a ruined temple: Veyra wants the Seal reforged under divine rule; the hollow god Ossuar wants it destroyed so mortals stay prey. Tamsin and Dominic infiltrate disguised as pilgrims. The beat is escalating stakes and political horror among the divine.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Ossuar forces a partial unsealing: Tamsin relives her true childhood — she was a covenant-priest's daughter, willingly given up, her memory the payment that kept the realms closed. The beat is devastating clarity: her whole life was someone else's transaction.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Hunted by both factions, they descend into the Under Roads with a defrocked priest-guide, Maerin, who once served the original covenant. Maerin reveals the covenant was never meant to be divine property — it was co-authored with mortals. The beat is fragile hope and found-family warmth.

chapters.title: Maerin's Confession
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV (interlude). Maerin admits she helped draft the clause that made a child the seal — believing one life a fair price for peace. She gives Tamsin the original covenant text, half-eaten by rot. The beat is complicity examined: good intentions as their own kind of violence.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Veyra's hunters corner them on the salt flats; Dominic, powerless since exile, breaks his own oath and calls a storm anyway, nearly killing himself to buy escape. Tamsin shields him with a sigil and loses another year of memory. The beat is sacrifice compounding on sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Empty Journal
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Reading her own journal, Tamsin finds entries she doesn't remember writing and one that terrifies her: a plan, in her handwriting, to give herself wholly to Veyra. She must decide whether her past selves can be trusted with her future. The beat is identity as argument with oneself.

chapters.title: Terms of Reforging
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. With Maerin's fragmentary text, Dominic drafts a new covenant: gods answer only freely-given prayer, bound not by a person but by distributed mortal memory — thousands of keepers instead of one seal. The beat is intellectual climax: the problem reframed from power to consent.

chapters.title: Veyra's Last Offer
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Veyra makes a final offer: restore every stolen memory, whole and perfect, if Tamsin accepts the old seal and divine stewardship forever. Tamsin sees the trap — a complete self purchased at the cost of every future choice. The beat is the theme crystallized: identity requires the right to change.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At the Worldspine altar, Tamsin begins the ritual to dissolve the seal — Ossuar attacks mid-rite, Veyra turns on them all, and Dominic holds the storm-line alone while Maerin dies buying them seconds. The beat is full-throttle climax: everything staked, allies falling.

chapters.title: Written in Mortal Memory
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Dying, Tamsin scatters the covenant into the minds of everyone who ever prayed sincerely — including strangers in the valley below — making the pact unownable. Her sigils fade to faint scars. The beat is transcendence through relinquishment: power given away becomes law.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Quiet Gods
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The gods withdraw into distant, bounded roles; prayers are answered rarely and gently. Dominic, pardoned but purposeless, chooses to return to the valley rather than reclaim his old glory. The beat is decompression and quiet reckoning with what survival cost them both.

chapters.title: Tamsin and the Sigil
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Back in the Hollow Valley, Tamsin reopens the candle shop with faded scars and a journal full of recovered fragments — some memories returned, some gone forever, and that, she decides, is honest. A child asks about her scar; she says it's a signature. The beat is resolution: identity as something you keep writing, not something you recover.
